name: Camera pan, tilt and zoom control
plain: Lets a site move or zoom a PTZ-capable camera.
meaning: Gives the site physical control of camera direction and zoom on conferencing cameras, so it can aim at people and rooms. Gated by a separate permission on top of camera access.

web.api: getUserMedia({video: {pan: true, tilt: true, zoom: true}}); track.applyConstraints({advanced: [{pan, tilt, zoom}]}); getCapabilities()

access.prompt_ui: Chrome shows a distinct prompt when constraints request pan, tilt or zoom: Allow control of camera movements. Granting unlocks all three on that device.
access.persistence: Stored with the camera permission per origin
steps: Request video with panTiltZoom permission descriptor

data.metric: Camera pan, tilt and zoom settings

limits.headline: Can move or zoom a motorized camera, once the site already has camera access
limits.user_action: You use pan or zoom controls on a video call or monitoring page and approve the extra prompt
can: Pan, tilt and zoom a camera that has those motors or lenses
Change the framing during a call or while watching a feed
Use all three movements on that camera after one approval
cannot: Move a camera that has no motor or zoom
Control the camera without the separate camera movement prompt in Chrome
Grant only zoom and keep pan locked; the approval covers all three
Work in Firefox, Safari or iPhone browsers, which do not offer it
limits.reach_label: One camera, while you use the site
limits.differs: Works in Chrome and Edge (desktop and Android). Firefox, Safari and iPhone browsers do not support it.

story.what_it_is: Lets a site tilt, turn and zoom a motorized camera, not only look through it.

marketing.name: Camera pan, tilt and zoom
marketing.pitch: Chrome explains that web apps can steer PTZ webcams for conferencing, with a separate permission from plain camera access.

story.for_you: If you have a camera that can move, such as a conference room camera, a second prompt asks whether the site may point and zoom it. If you say yes, you may see the camera swing toward a speaker without anyone touching it.
story.for_makers: Meeting and telehealth sites want to frame people well and follow whoever talks, without a separate control app. A web page can then run a whole room camera system. It also saves support calls about camera setup.

use_cases.example: A web based room system in a boardroom zooms in on whoever is talking, so remote staff can see faces and not a wide table shot.
A doctor on a telehealth site zooms the patient camera onto a rash or a wound so the care team can see detail from far away.
A lecture hall camera follows the teacher around the room while students watch the stream in a browser tab.
A church or school streams a service on the web, and the volunteer pans the camera from a browser page on a laptop.
A shop owner opens a web page that lets them aim a motorized store camera at the door or the till from home.
A pet camera page lets you swivel and zoom to find your cat, using a plain browser tab on your phone.
A tabletop board game stream lets the host steer an overhead camera to show the cards on the table to remote players.

risks: Camera aimed at people without their notice
Gives a site physical control of hardware

technical_bounds: Only works on cameras that advertise PTZ

abuse: Remotely aiming a camera at people after capture is granted

history.change: Camera PTZ control ships behind a permission
